         EXCEPTIONS TO THE PFD OF INTERVENORS THE MOSELEY GROUP
                    AND THE V8 LANDOWNERS COALITION

          Intervenors James Gregory Waller, Marilyn Moseley Waller, Arthur Kyle Moseley, David

Moseley (Moseley Group) and the V8 Landowners Coalition submit these Exceptions to the

Proposal for Decision (PFD). These parties will at times be called the “Multiple Intervenors” in

these Exceptions.


                                     SUMMARY OF EXCEPTIONS

          Multiple Intervenors agree with the PFD that if a route should be selected, Route 894 best
complies with PUC criteria. They are filing these Exceptions to avoid any possible waiver before
the Commissioners regarding the PFD’s suggestion that Route 392 performs better on
environmental considerations. Route 392 uses Link U3 to cross the Colorado River, and the
evidence demonstrated that Route 894’s crossing of the Colorado River using Link J22 is superior
to the Link U3 crossing. These Exceptions express no position on issues other than route selection.

             JURISDICTION, PROCEDURAL HISTORY, APPLICABLE LAW,
    PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES (1-4), DUE PROCESS, AND NEED (ISSUES 5-7)


          Multiple Intervenors take no position on these matters and have no exceptions.


                                 ISSUE NOS. 8-10; ROUTE SELECTION

          Multiple Intervenors agree that Route 894 best meets all applicable PUC criteria. With

respect to the specific issue of the Colorado River crossing’s environmental concerns, Multiple

Intervenors disagree with the PFD’s statement that Route 392 performs favorably on

environmental considerations because it utilizes “a Colorado River Crossing with a pre-existing

infrastructure corridor.1” The evidence demonstrated that on this issue as well, Route 894 is

superior.

          As shown from the admitted exhibits, Route 894’s Link J22 will cross in a perpendicular

manner and not run parallel to the Colorado River2. In sharp contrast, U3’s crossing is not

perpendicular; U3 runs parallel to the Colorado River for almost two miles3. The PFD specifically

noted the value of Route 894 not running parallel to any streams4.

          U3 crosses at an ecologically significant stream segment (ESSS)5; Link J22 does not6. U3

crosses at USFWS critical habitat7; J22 does not8. Only U3 crosses within the North-Central

Prairies major land resource area (MLRA)9, where most of the rainfall occurs during high-intensity

intensity convective thunderstorms elevates the risk of simultaneous outages11. Finally, U3 crosses

an area with multiple river bends12; J22 does not13.

          Route 392’s crossing at a location with an existing transmission line crossing is at best

neutral; the aesthetic advantages are offset by the risks of simultaneous outages14 in an area much

more prone to experience high-intensity convective thunderstorms15. As to multiple other

environmental considerations, Route 894 is superior to 392.

   OTHER PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES (ISSUES 11-16), UNCONTESTED
MATTERS, SUMMARY, FINDINGS OF FACT, CONCLUSIONS OF LAW, PROPOSED
                     ORDERING PARAGRAPHS


          Multiple Intervenors agree with and support Findings 156-250. As to other Findings,

Multiple Intervenors take no position and have no exceptions.

                                              CONCLUSION

          Multiple Intervenors urge the ALJs to issue an Exceptions Letter stating, “Route 392

utilizes a Colorado River crossing with a pre-existing infrastructure corridor; however, the specific

infrastructure is an existing transmission line. This proximity would increase the risk of

simultaneous outages and more severe electric grid disruptions. Regarding other environmental

considerations, Route 894’s Colorado River crossing (Link J22) is superior to Route 392’s

crossing.”
